title: Intimacy Pact
concept: An agreement for initiating and declining physical closeness, so saying no never costs either of you anything, and what each of you actually wants doesn’t stay a guess.
whenToUse: Set it up in advance, when initiating or declining feels tense, when it’s stalled for weeks, or after a breach that touched this part of the relationship.
steps: Before you initiate, think about how it lands for the other person. If you’re declining, you owe nothing: just say no.
Say out loud: neither of you will punish, sulk, or guilt-trip the other for declining. A no costs nothing and needs no reason.

If it helps, agree on warm-no wording and an alternative you’d both genuinely enjoy — holding each other, a kiss goodnight, five minutes of talking. Optional, never owed: a no needs no script, reason, or substitute offer.
Each of you names what you actually enjoy and how you like to be approached: body language can signal interest, but a clear yes is still asked for.
Revisit the agreement every 30 days. Update it as things change — it’s not a one-time contract, and nobody keeps score in between.

If a no has been met with pressure or guilt-tripping, stop here and have a Green Rule or Trust Recovery conversation first — don’t try to patch intimacy on top of that. If it involved force, threats or fear, it isn’t a ‘once’: go straight to the Help Lines. If it happens again, or either of you feels unable to say no, stop and use the Help Lines.

phrases.text: I want to be close — not in that space tonight. Can we hold each other?
Not about you. Can we do something together instead?
Not tonight — I do want to be near you. Is that okay?

working: B says no, plainly. A says “okay” and means it: no cold shoulder, no guilt trip, no sulk at breakfast. Next time, asking still feels easy for both.
notWorking: A no that gets a flat “fine” and the silent treatment — or someone initiating without a thought for whether the other person is up for it. That’s what makes this feel unsafe to be honest about.
activity: Write the agreement together — there’s a worksheet for this — and put a real date on the calendar for the 30-day check-in.
warn: A “no” needs no script, reason, or substitute offer. No pact or agreement creates an obligation to sex, touch, or disclosure. If a no is met with pressure again, or either of you feels unable to say no, stop and use the Help Lines.
